title: Transformations on the Cartesian Plane: Reflections, Rotations and Translations
seo_title: Year 7 Transformations Worksheets: Reflections, Rotations and Translations on the Cartesian Plane (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: describe transformations of a set of points using coordinates in the Cartesian plane, translations and reflections on an axis, and rotations about a given point
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on transformations for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7SP03): reflections in the axes, rotations about a point, translations, transforming shapes and describing transformations. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Reflection: mirror line. Rotation: angle, direction, centre. Translation: how far across and up or down.
key_sub: Reflections, rotations and translations keep the shape the same size (congruent).
body_html:
How it works

  • Reflection in the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). In the y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y).
  • Rotation: give the angle, the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) and the centre. 180° about the origin: (x, y) → (−x, −y).
  • Translation: every point slides the same way, such as 3 units right and 2 units down.

All three keep the shape the same size and shape, so the image is congruent.

Example

Reflect (3, −2) in the y-axis.

Change the sign of the x-coordinate.

Answer: (−3, −2)

Example

Translate (1, 4) 3 units right and 5 units down.

1 + 3 = 4 and 4 − 5 = −1.

Answer: (4, −1)

Example

Rotate (2, 5) 180° about the origin.

Change both signs.

Answer: (−2, −5)

Common mistakes

  • Reflecting in the wrong axis: the x-axis is horizontal, so reflecting in it changes the y-coordinate.
  • Rotating the wrong way: anticlockwise is the opposite way to clock hands.
  • Swapping the moves: right and left change x; up and down change y.
  • Forgetting the centre of rotation when it is not the origin.

faq.q: What happens to coordinates when you reflect in the x-axis?
How do I describe a rotation?
faq.a: Give the angle (such as 90° or 180°), the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) and the centre of rotation.

faq.q: How do I translate a point?
faq.a: Add the move across to the x-coordinate and the move up or down to the y-coordinate. Left and down are negative.
Exactly the same size and shape. Reflections, rotations and translations always give a congruent image.

items.q: The point (−4, −3) is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (−4, 3).

items.q: The point (2, 4) is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (−2, 4).

items.q: The point (3, 3) is rotated 90° clockwise about the point (2, 0). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (1, 3) from the centre becomes (3, −1). Image: (5, −1).

items.q: The point (−4, 3) is rotated 180° about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Rotating 180° about the origin changes both signs. Image: (4, −3).

items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (3, 5) from the centre becomes (5, −3). Image: (7, −3).

items.q: The point (1, 5) is translated 5 units right and 4 units down. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving right changes the x-coordinate by 5; moving down changes the y-coordinate by −4. Image: (6, 1).

items.q: The point (0, 3) is translated to (−4, 5). Describe the translation.
items.e: x: 0 → −4 is −4. y: 3 → 5 is 2. 4 units left and 2 units up.

items.q: The point (1, −1) is translated 3 units right and 1 unit down. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving right changes the x-coordinate by 3; moving down changes the y-coordinate by −1. Image: (4, −2).

items.q: The point (1, −5) is translated 3 units right and 1 unit up. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving right changes the x-coordinate by 3; moving up changes the y-coordinate by 1. Image: (4, −4).

items.q: The point (−2, 3) is translated 3 units right and 6 units down. Where is its image?
items.e: Moving right changes the x-coordinate by 3; moving down changes the y-coordinate by −6. Image: (1, −3).

items.q: The point (−2, 5) is translated 3 units left and 6 units down. Where is its image?

items.e: Moving left changes the x-coordinate by −1; moving up changes the y-coordinate by 6. Image: (−2, 6).

items.q: The point (5, −3) is translated to (1, −8). Describe the translation.
items.e: x: 5 → 1 is −4. y: −3 → −8 is −5. 4 units left and 5 units down.

items.q: The point (−3, 0) is translated to (−4, −5). Describe the translation.
items.e: x: −3 → −4 is −1. y: 0 → −5 is −5. 1 unit left and 5 units down.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 2), B(5, 2), C(2, 4). It is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(2, 2) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin, so A′ is (2, −2).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, 3), B(5, 3), C(3, 5). It is rotated 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of B′?
items.e: B(5, 3) is rotated 180° about the origin, so B′ is (−5, −3).

items.e: B(3, 3) is translated 4 units left and 3 units up, so B′ is (−1, 6).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 1), B(4, 1), C(1, 3). It is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(1, 1) is reflected in the y-axis, so A′ is (−1, 1).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, 3), B(5, 3), C(3, 5). It is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of B′?

items.e: C(1, 6) is translated 4 units left and 3 units up, so C′ is (−3, 9).

items.e: B(4, 3) is translated 3 units right and 5 units down, so B′ is (7, −2).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 2), B(4, 2), C(2, 5). It is translated 3 units right and 2 units up. What are the coordinates of C′?

items.q: Shape A (blue) is mapped onto shape B (red). Describe the single transformation.
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: B is the mirror image of A across the y-axis: a reflection in the y-axis.

items.q: Shape A (blue) is mapped onto shape B (red). Describe the single transformation.
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: B is upside down in the opposite quadrant: a rotation of 180° about the origin.

items.q: Shape A (blue) is mapped onto shape B (red). Describe the single transformation.
c: A translation 4 units left and 5 units down
A translation 5 units left and 4 units down
items.e: Every point moves 5 left and 4 down: a translation 5 units left and 4 units down.

items.q: Shape A (blue) is mapped onto shape B (red). Describe the single transformation.
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
items.e: B is the mirror image of A across the x-axis: a reflection in the x-axis.

items.q: Shape A (blue) is mapped onto shape B (red). Describe the single transformation.
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Each point (x, y) goes to (y, −x): a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin.

items.q: After a reflection, rotation or translation, the image is…
items.e: These keep every length and angle, so the image is congruent.

items.q: To describe a rotation fully, you must give…
c: The angle, the direction and the centre
items.e: A full description needs the angle, the direction and the centre.

items.q: Which point does not move when it is reflected in the x-axis?
items.e: Points on the mirror line stay where they are: (4, 0).

items.q: A shape is rotated 90° clockwise and then another 90° clockwise about the same centre. What single rotation is this?
Which is the same as a rotation of 270° anticlockwise?
items.e: 270° one way ends in the same place as 90° the other way.

items.q: The point (5, 2) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Where is its image?
A point (2, −3) is reflected in the line x = 4. Where is its image?
items.e: 2 is 2 left of the line, so the image is 2 right of it: (6, −3).

items.q: Which transformation could map the letter b onto the letter d?
c: A reflection in a vertical line
items.e: b and d are mirror images: a reflection in a vertical line.

items.q: Which transformation could map the letter b onto the letter q?
c: A reflection in a vertical line
items.e: Turning b upside down gives q: a rotation of 180°.

items.q: A translation moves (1, 1) to (4, −2). Where does the same translation move (0, 5)?
items.e: The move is 3 right and 3 down: (0 + 3, 5 − 3) = (3, 2).

items.q: Reflecting in the y-axis changes…
items.e: The y-axis is vertical, so points move left or right: the sign of the x-coordinate changes.

items.q: Rotating 180° about the origin changes…
items.e: (x, y) → (−x, −y): both signs change.

items.q: A shape is reflected in the x-axis and then reflected again in the x-axis. Where does it end up?
items.e: Two reflections in the same line undo each other: back where it started.

items.q: Which coordinates show a square's corner (3, 1) after a translation 4 units left?
A game character at (−2, 3) moves 5 right and 6 down. Where is it now?
